Subject: Private edge: network ownership handoff and operational checklist

Hi Raj,

Thanks again for the productive preflight last week. Attached is a concise handoff checklist we typically use when ownership for a private edge/VPC connection transfers to the customer networking team. See the attached: redwood_private_handoff_checklist_v1.pdf and acme-network-diagram-v1.png.

Key asks from our side to help lock schedule:
- Confirm the maintenance window for cutover (we've penciled Tue 2026-11-16 02:00-05:00 UTC).
- Provide the canonical CIDR ranges for your peering/VPN endpoints and the public egress IPs we'll allow.
- Confirm the service account email we should expect to be allowed in IAM and the KMS key alias for envelope encryption (if using customer-managed keys).

Next steps: once you confirm CIDR + service account + window we will schedule a 60-min technical walkthrough with Karthik and the edge ops team.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment(s): redwood_private_handoff_checklist_v1.pdf (pdf), acme-network-diagram-v1.png (image)

Subject: Re: Private edge: network ownership handoff and operational checklist

Markus,

Appreciate the checklist — looks comprehensive. Quick answers:
- Maintenance window: Tue 2026-11-16 02:00-04:00 UTC works for us.
- CIDRs: 10.240.0.0/16 for internal service, 198.51.100.0/24 for egress NAT pool.
- Service account: infra-acme@acmehealth.com
- KMS: we will use cmk-acme-01 (customer-managed).

We do have one ask: can Redwood confirm what logs you will ship back to us and retention? Also want to ensure any debug-level dumps are off by default.

Happy to jump on the walkthrough — Thurs 2026-11-05 15:00 PST works.

Thanks,
Raj
Network Lead — Acme Health
raj.patel@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: network ownership handoff and operational checklist

Raj — perfect, thanks for the details. Quick bullets to confirm alignment before the call:
- We'll configure observed egress as 198.51.100.0/24 and allow inbound peering from 10.240.0.0/16.
- Logs: we provide connection-level events, per-request latency/trace summaries, and optional audit exports. Default retention is 30 days; exports to your S3/GCS can be set to match your retention policies. Detailed export config will be included in the walkthrough notes.
- Debug dumps are off by default; storage of any full traces requires explicit consent and a retention tag.

For the walkthrough on Thu 2026-11-05 15:00 PST I propose this agenda:
1) Quick introductions + roles (10m)
2) Network diagram walk-through & IP mapping (15m)
3) KMS and key rotation expectations (10m)
4) Logging/export/retention options (10m)
5) Cutover plan & rollback triggers (15m)

I've attached a lightweight routing PSA (routing-psa.docx) that summarizes NAT/egress behavior for edge nodes.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): routing-psa.docx (docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: network ownership handoff and operational checklist

Quick technical notes for the prep docs and smoke tests we will run during the walkthrough:

Required firewall/NAT rules (customer-managed):
- Allow TCP 443 outbound to Redwood collector endpoints: collector.use.redwood.ai:443 (egress allow list: 198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.11).
- Allow TCP 22 from our maintenance IPs only for occasional support sessions (we will request temporary access via tickets).
- Allow UDP 53 for DNS to your resolver or allow our resolver IPs.

Preflight smoke tests (examples we'll run):
- curl -v https://collector.use.redwood.ai/healthz (expect 200 and TLS chain validated)
- traceroute -n collector.use.redwood.ai (confirm path and egress IP)
- curl --resolve agent.acme:443:<your-egress-ip> https://agent.acme/ops (confirm hostname/IP mapping)

BGP/Peering notes: if you plan a routed peering instead of simple VPN, please share ASN and BGP neighbor IPs ahead of time.

Also: if you opt to use customer-managed KMS (cmk-acme-01), we need a one-time IAM binding for our service account infra-acme@acmehealth.com to be allowed encrypt/decrypt using the key.

I'll bring a template runbook to the call so we can edit in real time.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
